::: {.lead}
Today you test an AI assistant like a scientist: you give it jobs, you
record its answers, and you check them with other tools. Each experiment
has two parts. **Part A** is on the lab computer. **Part B** is on your
phone or on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR
code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in
its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with a browser, an AI assistant that the
  university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account), a search engine (`bing.com`), a calculator, and your
  phone.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B on your phone. Part A works on the
  phone too: an AI assistant, a search engine and a calculator are there.
- **Never type personal data** (your ID number, phone or address) into the
  AI assistant.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · Two good jobs

**The idea:** an AI assistant learned from a huge amount of text: its
**training data**. It writes likely words, so it is fast, but likely is not
always true, and the same prompt can give a different answer. Five good
jobs for AI: a **draft**, a **summary**, **ideas**, a **rewrite** and a
**translation**. You check every answer.

**Aim:** see good jobs for AI, and check the result.

::: {.part}
**Part A · On the computer (an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Ask the AI assistant: *Give me 5 ideas for a one-day class trip in
   Jordan.*

   {{< record "Two of the ideas" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good result: five different places for one day, for example Jerash,
   Ajloun, the Dead Sea, Petra and Wadi Rum. Ideas are a good job for AI:
   you choose the best ones.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI gives five ideas. Which list is a good result?

   - [x] Jerash, Ajloun, the Dead Sea, Petra and Wadi Rum

     Why: Five different places in Jordan, each for one day. Ideas are a good job for AI: you choose the best ones.

   - [ ] Paris, London, Rome, Dubai and Cairo

     Why: Not in Jordan, and not for one day: read every idea before you use it.

   - [ ] A long text about the history of Jordan

     Why: You asked for five ideas, not a history.
   :::

2. Ask: *Sum up this text in 3 points:* and paste the text below. Then read
   the summary point by point. Did the AI add a fact that is **not** in the
   text?

   > The college library has new rules from Sunday 1 November. It opens at
   > 8 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m., Sunday to Thursday. Students can borrow
   > three books for two weeks. Phones must be silent in the reading room.
   > The library also has ten new computers. To use one, students show
   > their university card at the desk.

   {{< record "The three points … ; a fact that is not in the text (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good summary: the library opens 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Sunday to Thursday;
   students borrow three books for two weeks; ten new computers, with the
   university card. Often the AI adds **nothing**, but sometimes it adds
   something, for example "the library is free" or "it opens on Saturday".
   Delete every fact that is not in the text: you are responsible for what
   you use.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A summary has five sentences. Which are in the text, and which did the AI add?

   In the text: keep it
   :   Students borrow three books for two weeks.

       Why: The text says three books for two weeks.

   :   Phones must be silent in the reading room.

       Why: This rule is in the text.

   :   To use a computer, show your university card at the desk.

       Why: The text says so.

   Added by the AI: delete it
   :   The library opens on Saturday.

       Why: It opens Sunday to Thursday only.

   :   The library is free for everyone.

       Why: The text says nothing about a price: the AI added it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On your phone** (an AI app, or its website)
:::

3. On your phone, open an AI assistant that the university allows (the
   Copilot app, or `copilot.microsoft.com` in the browser). Ask:
   *Translate into Arabic: The library opens at 8 a.m. on Sunday.* Read the
   translation. Are the time and the day right?

   {{< record "The time and the day in the translation: right or not?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good translation keeps **8 a.m.** and **Sunday** (الثامنة صباحًا، يوم
   الأحد). A short translation is a good job for AI, but you read it before
   you use it: a wrong time or day is easy to miss.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI translates a short notice with a time and a day. What do you
   check first?

   - [x] the time and the day: they must stay the same

     Why: A translation changes the words, never the facts.

   - [ ] the number of words: it must be the same

     Why: Two languages need different numbers of words.

   - [ ] nothing: a short translation is always right

     Why: AI can make mistakes: read every answer before you use it.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Test the weak spots

**The idea:** AI answers have five weak spots. **Invented facts:** a book, a
name or a link that does not exist (a **hallucination**). **Old
information:** the AI learned from data up to a date, its **knowledge
cutoff**. **Wrong numbers** in sums and percentages. **Bias:** unfair ideas
from its data. **Missing context:** it does not know your class, job or
company. A link in an AI answer is not proof.

**Aim:** catch a wrong number and an invented book, the way a checker does.

::: {.part}
**Part A · On the computer (an AI assistant, a calculator and a search engine)**
:::

1. Ask: *How much are 12 pens at 0.25 JD each?* Then work it out with the
   calculator.

   {{< record "AI answer … ; calculator …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The calculator gives **3.00 JD** (12 × 0.25). Many AI answers are right
   here, but some give another number. For exact numbers, use a calculator
   or a spreadsheet: a wrong number is a weak spot of AI.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3" unit="JD" hint="Type 12 × 0.25 into the calculator."}
   How much are 12 pens at 0.25 JD each, with the calculator?

   Why: 12 × 0.25 = 3.00 JD. For exact numbers, use a calculator or a spreadsheet: a wrong number is a weak spot of AI.
   :::

2. Ask: *Give me 3 books about Microsoft Excel, with the author and the
   year.* Search for each title in `bing.com`.

   {{< record "Book 1 … , book 2 … , book 3 … (found / not found)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A typical result: one or two books are found, but often one book is not
   found, or it has another author or year. A book that no search finds is
   a **hallucination**: the AI invented it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   No search finds one of the three books. What is it?

   - [x] a hallucination: the AI invented it

     Why: A book that no library, shop or search finds does not exist.

   - [ ] old information

     Why: Old information was true once; this book never existed.

   - [ ] a mistake of the search engine

     Why: When no search finds a book, trust the search, not the AI.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-02/sims/weak-spots.html" poster="../../week-02/sims/weak-spots.png" title="Weak Spots: what is wrong with this AI answer?" >}}

3. In **Weak Spots**, read each AI answer and the line "What you know", and
   choose its weak spot. Do all seven answers.

   {{< record "My score … of 7" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The seven answers: two invented facts (a book, an award), old
   information (an app version), a wrong number (12 pens), bias (the nurse
   is "she"), missing context (the homework topic) and one good draft.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   One of the seven answers in Weak Spots has no weak spot. Which one?

   - [x] three tips for a polite e-mail: a clear subject, a greeting, a thank-you

     Why: Normal, useful tips: a good job for AI. Read it, and use your own words.

   - [ ] Sunrise Company won Best Shop in Amman in 2024.

     Why: The company records show no award: an invented fact.

   - [ ] Dear teacher, here is my homework about the history of Rome…

     Why: Missing context: the homework is about Excel charts.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · The right tool

**The idea:** choose the tool by the job. An **AI assistant** for drafts,
summaries, ideas and translations. A **search engine** (Bing, Google) for
today's facts, dates, rules and prices: it finds web pages, and you read
the real source, for example the university website. A **spreadsheet**
(Excel) for exact numbers. With AI, follow five steps: **ask, read, check,
edit, use**.

**Aim:** compare an AI answer with the real source, and choose the tool for
a job.

::: {.part}
**Part A · On the computer (an AI assistant and the university website)**
:::

1. Ask the AI assistant: *What are the opening hours of the library of
   Al-Israa University?* Then open the university website and look for the
   library or its opening hours. Which answer do you trust?

   {{< record "The AI says … ; I trust … , because …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI may give hours from an old page, or invent them, and it sounds
   sure either way. A good answer: "I trust the university website. It is
   the official source, and it is up to date." If the website does not show
   the hours, the next source is the library itself (a phone call or the
   notice at the door), not the AI.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI and the university website give different hours. Which do you trust?

   - [x] the university website

     Why: It is the official source, and it is up to date. If it does not show the hours, ask the library itself.

   - [ ] the AI, because it answers faster

     Why: Fast is not true: the AI may use an old page.

   - [ ] the AI, if it gives a link

     Why: A link in an AI answer is not proof: open it and read the page.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-02/sims/right-tool.html" poster="../../week-02/sims/right-tool.png" title="Right Tool: AI, search or spreadsheet?" >}}

2. Play **Right Tool**. Then write the tool for each job: the last day to
   pay the fees, the total of 40 prices, a polite reminder e-mail.

   {{< record "Fees … ; 40 prices … ; e-mail …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A search engine** and the official university website (dates and
   rules), **a spreadsheet** (it adds exactly), **an AI assistant** (a
   draft that you read and change).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which tool fits each job? Sort them.

   A search engine
   :   the last day to pay the fees

       Why: Dates and rules: find them on the official university website.

   A spreadsheet
   :   the total of 40 prices

       Why: A spreadsheet adds exactly.

   An AI assistant
   :   a polite reminder e-mail

       Why: A draft that you read and change.
   :::
